svg.text: Memory map: what each address means
Loads and stores reach memory and devices; CSR instructions reach the registers inside the core. Same map in simulation and on the FPGA.
never cached, never stored to RAM
then its data; programs set their own sp
loaded by the firmware ("l") on the FPGA,
main memory: 64 KiB (addresses wrap every 64 KiB)
Device registers at 0x1000_0000 + offset (8 bytes each; use ld / sd, or sb for PUTCHAR)
print one character (UART on the FPGA)
bit0 byte waiting, bit1 queue full, bit2 idle, 15:8 byte
set it: interrupt at MTIME >= it
In simulation the timer works everywhere; the other device loads return 0 and only PUTCHAR (and LEDS, in the
model) do anything, so the same program runs unchanged on the model, the RTL and the board.
Control and status registers: a separate address space, inside the core (csrr / csrw)
L F R K I D: the bubble counters of the cycle equation
trap setup: interrupt enable bits, handler address
where a trap happened and why (ecall, ebreak)
interrupt enables / pending: bit 7 timer, bit 11 external
write 1: PASS, (n << 1) | 1: FAIL test n / interrupts taken
